locator_policy: Section, table and figure references point into the cited arXiv version. locator_status is one of: verified (re-checked against retrieved text), provisional (known section, not re-checked), unavailable (no locator can be produced from material currently in the tree). claims.claim_text: The three static analysis tools achieved average F1 scores of 0.260 (SonarQube), 0.386 (CodeQL) and 0.546 (SnykCode).

witness.quote: The language-based scanners achieve higher mean F-1 scores,0.797, 0.753 and 0.750, than their static counterparts, which score 0.260, 0.386 and 0.546, respectively.

claims.notes: Verified in the remediation pass against the retrieved arXiv HTML. Previously the tool-to-score mapping was inferred from abstract ordering and recorded as such; the paper states the mapping explicitly, so the inference has been replaced by a quotable sentence. Witness quote and offset recorded against retrieval D3-2026-11-06-abs.

claims.claim_text: The three LLMs achieved average F1 scores of 0.797 (GPT-4.1), 0.753 (Mistral Large) and 0.750 (DeepSeek V3).

witness.quote: The language-based scanners achieve higher mean F-1 scores,0.797, 0.753 and 0.750, than their static counterparts, which score 0.260, 0.386 and 0.546, respectively.

claims.notes: Same sentence pair as D3-C01. Witness quote and offset recorded against retrieval D3-2026-11-06-abs.

claims.claim_text: The LLMs' advantage over static tools originates in higher recall rather than higher precision.

witness.quote: LLMs' advantage originates from superior recall, confirming an ability to reason across broader code contexts.

claims.notes: Present in the retrieved abstract text. Witness quote and offset recorded against retrieval D3-2026-11-06-abs.

claims.claim_text: All three LLMs reported an incorrect line and column region while correctly identifying the vulnerable file, and the authors attribute this to tokenisation.
claims.notes: Recorded during acquisition; locator not re-verified in this pass. This claim drives the content-anchored finding design (S1), so it must be locator-verified before S1 is treated as evidence-backed.

claims.claim_text: Semgrep was used as an external oracle against standard vulnerability benchmarks and disagreed with the benchmark labels in both directions.
claims.notes: The load-bearing claim of the whole project. Locator must be re-established before the label-provenance architecture is described as evidence-driven.

claims.claim_text: Whether current LLMs can detect vulnerabilities at all is reported as unclear.
claims.notes: In tension with D2 and D3 reported F1 scores; recorded as a contradiction in 03.

claims.claim_text: The systematic literature review covers 263 primary studies.
claims.notes: Count taken during acquisition; locator not re-established.

claims.claim_text: Agentic review teams and uncertainty-gated routing to human reviewers are documented existing practice.
claims.notes: This claim is what forces the novelty framing to narrow, so it carries unusual weight for an unverified claim.

claims.claim_text: LLM-based vulnerability detection systems report F1 scores approaching 0.9 on standard benchmarks.
claims.notes: Survey-secondhand figure. Even when verified, this is a report of others' results, not a replicated finding.

claims.claim_text: Static analysis tools are widely used as ground truth in vulnerability detection evaluation despite being imperfect oracles.
claims.notes: Recorded as author interpretation, not as a measured result.
